newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRM ON CENTRAL BANK SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRM ON CENTRAL BANK SUPPORT.

text.p: Zimbabwe's central Reserve Bank (RBZ) intervened heavily on Friday to stop the Zimbabwe dollar from falling too steeply against major currencies, and may do so again next week, foreign exchange dealers said on Friday.
"The bank stepped in, in a very heavy way, and by the end of the day, the (Zimbabwe) dollar had gained three cents on its morning level on the U.S. dollar," one dealer said.
"The way they came in today may be an indication they will continue supporting it next week if the pressure continues."
The Zimbabwe dollar has been under severe speculation and import pressure this week, losing 15 cents against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, in a market that saw little central bank intervention.

The Zimbabwe dollar closed Friday at 10.6900/7100 from Thursday's close 10.7200/7400 against the U.S. dollar, and at 17.0150/0550 on sterling from 17.0130/0550 and on the mark at 6.9350/9510 from 6.9670/9810.
It was quoted firmer on the rand at 2.3460/3530 compared to 2.3530/3590.
